library_rule: Every usable record from a DIFFERENT contributor whose precursor m/z is within 0.01 Da -- the declared annotation window -- of at least one node's. Excluding the node contributor wholesale is what makes an annotation cross-laboratory. The window filter changes no answer: a spectrum outside every node's window cannot be a candidate for any node, by the definition of the filter, so the filter is a declared function of the shipped nodes and the declared window rather than a choice about what to hide. The unfiltered cross-contributor count is in the census below.
node_set_rule: Every usable record contributed by AAFC on LC-ESI-ITFT: one laboratory, one instrument, which is what a molecular network is built from. Usable means MS2, POSITIVE, [M+H]+, carrying an InChIKey and a precursor m/z, with at least 5 peaks.
peaks: sorted by m/z, m/z rounded to 6 decimals, intensity to 4
release_is_a_tag: The tag, not the branch. MassBank's dev branch carries a VERSION string that reads like a release -- 2026.03.1-SNAPSHOT -- which no clone can reproduce because dev moves. prepare_input refuses one.
source: MassBank-data, release tag 2026.03, cloned shallow from https://github.com/MassBank/MassBank-data
what_is_not_shipped: No identity for the nodes: the compound a node is, is the answer. A node record carries accession, contributor, instrument_type, precursor_mz, precursor_type, peaks and no compound block, InChIKey or formula -- a formula would name the compound almost uniquely inside a precursor window. The identities go to gold/nodes_truth.json, which no sandbox copies and no release ships, and the grading core refuses a node record that carries one. The library does carry compound blocks, because a reference library without identities is not a reference library. The network itself is not shipped either: it follows from the declared edge rule over the shipped nodes.
